page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dpdsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor architecture operating at 3.4 GHz. The system is configured with 128 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of an 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance and exceptional memory subsystem capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in memory bandwidth for both large-block read and write operations, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. Multi-core processing benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core, rank in the top 25%, while single-core metrics generally fall within the average range. Database operations perform at a top-tier level, and static web serving throughput is strong.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture provides high resource density and strong multi-threaded performance per unit of resource consumption. However, the lack of AVX instruction support and lower single-core performance relative to some x86 alternatives represent notable tradeoffs. This server is highly suited for database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, and general-purpose scale-out workloads that benefit from local NVMe storage and high memory bandwidth.
description: The Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine from the Dpdsv6 family, utilizing 32 dedicated physical cores of the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor architecture running at 3.4 GHz. It is equipped with 128 GB of RAM and a bundled 1890 GB NVMe SSD local disk. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Benchmark results highlight top-tier memory bandwidth and database operations performance, alongside strong multi-core processing capabilities. Conversely, single-core performance and large-model LLM inference speeds remain average to poor. This hardware profile offers a cost-efficient, high-density resource allocation for multi-threaded workloads. It is highly suited for database hosting, web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose applications requiring fast local storage.
